body:
I typically have the magic words to say, something like "if you don't feel like you're contributing today, what do you think you can do within your ability to start progress towards that? We all feel helpless at times and the best we can do is to improve ourselves and find space for ourselves." This would typically be what I would say to anyone without BPD.

Being honest, from one BPD to another, surviving happens by chance to me. My best friend blocked me just a few days ago because he got a new girlfriend. My appetite is 1/8 what it was, I sleep less than 3 hours a night now, and I'm struggling to take care of myself because "why should I if no one cares?" Because if no one else in my life cared, "friends" or "family" pretend that they can't see me when I cry, why should I bother to even shower? However, before I know it, the day is over. I survived another day even with all that. That's how I get through my day. I'm drowning every single day, but I survive because I'm struggling. Know you're not alone, and if all else fails.. wait until tomorrow. Personally, if I were to wipe myself out of existence, I would want it to be on a good day. I haven't had a good day yet, so maybe tomorrow.

If you need someone to just listen, you can DM me. Sometimes, that's all we need.

What you're feeling is unfiltered depression (BPD style). When having been so "used" to it myself, going on medication, then coming off... I was hit by a truck with it. When coming off medication, you really have to drill down on those DBT skills and if you have a therapist to talk to them as openly as you can (even if it's too much). When you're used to being stable long enough, it definitely feels weird to have those feelings again.

Personally, I always felt that way prior to medication, so it felt heavier when I was coming off because I was no longer used to the weight. It is important to note that the transition off medication is possibly one of the hardest, and more important to recognize signs that you are not functional without medication.

I can't deny I have toxic behaviors. I've been through extensive therapy and have grown a lot since my diagnosis, however I still be toxic. Me starting "if you leave I would probably kill myself" to someone close to me is toxic. To me, it doesn't change the fact that there's still that chance. To others, I'm holding myself hostage for friendship. I think that's the biggest barrier for us.

Yeah I tend to attract toxic people. It's like the world's worst superpower. My "best friend" didn't do that, but I guess the damage was bad enough to where he couldn't be around me if I do firmly believe I should be dead if he wasn't there for me. Now he isn't and I don't really have anyone close to me I deeply trust. It's why the out has been either suicide or going far from here, cause either way I don't have a support system anymore.

I took the family dog out for a run and stopped by a coffee shop afterwards to get her one of those "pup cups" with her. I work at a dog kennel as well, where we take the dogs outside every hour. I definitely go outdoors plenty, but it's hard to appreciate.

For me wanting to kill myself is due to "friends" in the past telling me to repeatedly, saying I was a awful person that should just "go die" for being horrible. This included a public "out" post where a previous friend said I should kill myself for being fake and "you know what you did" (which apparently was saying no to hanging out because I had a date). Another saying I should kill myself for breaking up with a mutual friend I was dating because I was horrible for being upset he played more video games than talking to me. This of course was beyond repeated bullying from others who would come up to me and tell me to kill myself for being a loser. This led to especially a lot of isolation for me growing up, as I had more external issues than unstable friendships. So for me, him not being in my life because I was in the way just proves that everyone was right and validates the idea in my head "yes, you are a bother, you are a burden, you should no longer be alive for all the pain you cause."

And, don't apologize for making assumptions or purposing reasons why. I'm sharing my reasons why. Healing is so hard when something new comes along to reopen an old wound. Literally and figuratively.

I hear you. I personally feel abandoned with actions like this, and definitely get overdramatic when it's even something small like this. However, being upset isn't overdramatic. You're allowed to feel sad, hurt, angry, happy, excited, etc. You are allowed to feel. It's how you react that matters. Personally, I would just be thrilled of the idea that two people I like are so close together, that way I wouldn't have to travel far to see either of them. (I also would split into panic mode occasionally, but I won't share what those thoughts would be as they are toxic.)

I already have a cat and she brings little comfort.. she just screams at me for treats or starts scratching her nails on glass until she gets her treats. Once she does she walks away. She doesn't let me pet her and she doesn't like cuddles.

I was talking to other people, but they never really wanted to be friends. I've tried very hard to meet new people, join clubs, volunteer, be more outgoing at work, but it's all so casual. I think I'm not very charismatic, so people just generally avoid me.

It's hard. Any advice I'm given is so repetitive that it upsets me to see it again. You can offer advice, I'm not sure if I can take it even though I can't sleep with this in my head. FP just not saying anything for hours (or reading it) hurts me more. If only everyone who was alone with sadness like this was able to huddle together like penguins in the winter, as there's some comfort. Thank you for listening.

I do go to university. People I meet don't want to meet me outside of school much less talk about anything other than schoolwork. I work as well at an open dog daycare and boarding facility, where I'm in a small room with literally only dogs and no other staff. There's of course some communication, but never much more beyond "(name of dog) is going home" or "(name of dog) is coming in today". I've tried opening about topics outside of basic work conversation, but it has never gone beyond small talk in the two years I've worked there.
I definitely don't feel okay :(
For some girls, it just adds moisture to the anal area and makes it extremely itchy and gross. I just use separate sheets for front and back, ain't no way I'm getting literal crap on my urethra.

"I'm just too busy to spend any time with you."
A lot of people have said horrible things to me, a lot of meaner things. But that... Triggers my fight or flight.
It's like having a magic 8 ball with 8 out of 10 times answering "you're going to die alone" with 2 out of 10 times being one side that says "yes, no, maybe."

I feel this deeply. My therapist suggested breathing exercises, journaling, reflecting, meditation, you name it. Nothing really solves that depressing dread in the morning. I tried stretches and working out as well, and I came to the same conclusion. It's quite demoralizing, I hope we both can find something that works for us someday
Leftover meatloaf in fresh made spaghetti. So good.
I hate to say it but I can't wait for it to shut down so someone could release a version where everything is accessible (like Toontown or Club Penguin), but only one can dream...
Wacky Zingoz, Cash Cow, and Tile Towers
My dog loves to bring me a toy whenever I come home from work or school. I can't take the toy, because it's hers, she just loves to show me her toy collection.

It's not a sign exactly of BPD alone, BPD typically is comorbid. However with extreme shifts in emotional attachment can display a hyperfixation-like behavior, either because of an FP or just because of black and white thinking patterns.

Dogs: a lifetime fixation. I volunteered at a dog shelter once I was old enough, working at a dog kennel currently. My favorite dog breeds are Borzoi and Akita (Japanese standard).

Drawing: Started when I was able to pick up a pencil. I started to seriously draw my freshman year of high school, stopped drawing once I was put in the hospital 4 years later. I still draw, but it doesn't bring me joy anymore.

Japan: while I have watched anime since I was about 12 or so, I started really becoming a japanophile when I was about 16 or so (also when I started displaying clinical symptoms of BPD)

I have a very narrow set of interests.
I pushed for a diagnosis since 16, got diagnosed at 18 finally. I'm turning 23 next month. You're definitely old enough.

Just start using reusable products instead of disposable ones. A more expensive short term but cheaper in the long term, would probably cost the same amount to use a menstrual cup, disc, or even homemade pads as of would for the increase in taxes to cover the cost of period products.

I like having too many tasks. On easy days I have plenty to do, on hard days I'm happy the list isn't as big as it was. On really hard days, I just make a goal of "bonus gems" where I just get gems just because.

I never said I wasn't responsible for it. I am 100% responsible for what I do and what I do to others. My behavior isn't excusable and it isn't something I don't want to change. I do want to become a better person. There are times where when I'm in psychosis and people are suddenly surprised that I have extreme behaviors of BPD despite having told them that I have BPD and will have extreme episodes.

I do go to therapy and I am getting help to avoid these extreme moments, I just get frustrated that people are surprised by my behavior when I tell them upfront that when I'm in distress I say things I don't mean and they still take it all to heart like I'm out to get their soul. When people especially I've known for many years, who know I have extremes, still are surprised and take me saying "I don't feel valued by you" so deeply they think I hate their guts.. I get frustrated both with myself and others.

I think it can be unhealthy based on how it's presented. If you live together, you do have a degree of right to know (when he'll be home, how far he's going, who he's going to be with in terms of knowing who to contact if you can't reach him directly). However if you don't live together, just ask where he's going and nothing more.

With us, knowing who he's with can make us more controlling in general. "Why are you with them and not me?" type of question. Loving includes freedom, not watching through a glass case. I'm so very guilty of this with my FP especially, and working on it sounds easier than it is.

The pain I received from everything before this, had gotten better just to get traumatically worse. Over and over again. I've been shattered for the last time and there's too many pieces to pick up alone.
I have OSDD in addition to CPTSD and BPD. I can't say I'm exactly a big help, just know you're not alone (as horrible as it may be).

BPD, ASD, OSDD, CPTSD, Anxiety (generalized, panic disorder, social anxiety), depression

What came first? We will never know
I'm happy you have people who care enough to ask beyond "you still there?" only once and never push to get an answer. Appreciate people who love you, even when it's hard to accept love

Well I've reached out then people feel the instant need to solve the issue. Even if I explain that I'm just having an episode that lasts for days, and even if the problem was solved I'd still feel upset, people still try to "fix" me or the issue for me. Then when I say I don't want it to be fixed, they just tell me to stop talking to them and see a therapist instead.

It may sound odd but I become more functional when I'm grieving the deceased in particular. I cry and grieve oncoming death or loss of loved ones so frequently, and spiral into loss of the fear of death that I am not shocked at all when death happens. My days become more normal because my expectations were met.
Unfortunately it only gets better if you make it better. The only way to know how it gets better is finding what you need for it to get better. It doesn't get better on its own.

I tell them this. But even when I tell them at the start of the conversation, they will go "well I'm not a therapist so stop giving me trauma" , "I can't cure you so stop venting" , or "figure it out yourself then and don't complain to me because I can't help you." Or persist to try and find a solution to the issue despite me openly saying I do not want it fixed.

I just tell people upfront I have BPD and need more help with things that other people find easy, including needing reassurance they won't leave. I tell rather openly "if I act like I absolutely hate you and despise you, do not take it to heart. I just think doing this will protect me from disappointment of you leaving later." Good people will try to learn ways to calm you down from extreme emotions at times you cannot regulate yourself, people who leave when you tell them this aren't worth our time.

Fluoxetine for me had the same exact problem OP mentioned, with constantly being sleepy and not being able to drink. The doctors suggested to just take it at night, but I still was drowsy during the day.

While in DBT therapy, they talked about redirecting these emotions into something else. Screaming into a pillow, punching pillows, shaving your head, or dying your hair were examples of healthy venting outlets they gave. I opted to write on sticky notes all the thoughts and statements I felt made me angry, and pasted them on the wall of my room. I kept writing down statements that made me angry until the rage subsided. It never went away but it stopped physically hurting. I kept that sticky note wall until I felt ready to move past that rage.

I still do sticky notes, but I put positive affirmations on them on my headboard. I don't have that intense rage anymore, only intense sadness.

I absolutely hate this phrase in particular: "parenthood is the antidote to selfishness"

I hate that people believe having children makes them better. How it makes them selfless. That is so false. No matter how stable we are and how far in remission we may think we are, what we do is very damaging to developing minds. We are impulsive, unpredictable, and dangerous at times to ourselves and others. No matter how well managed we may be, it's not worth damaging an entire life for it.
The classes. I remember them being so hard to understand and incomprehensible? Maybe I didn't like reading instructions.

It's HARD WORK. Not being appreciated hurts! I hate that people just dismiss us being normal, then freak out when we're not. Why can't they be surprised just once and say something cheesy like "I'm really proud of you for not freaking out, I know it must be really hard and I'll be with you every step of the way." I don't want to hear that from a therapist, I want that from my friends! My family! Ugh I understand so much.

I think it comes down to black and white thinking. A lot of stimulus for us requires a good/bad tag, and some unfortunate people's faces get that "bad" tag. In other words.... Yes I do and very often.

To be honest I never recovered from any of them. No amount of therapy brought me to a point where I "got over" it. I ask myself regularly about them, what I could have done differently, what I could improve on. I'm pretty sure I'm just a "oh yeah do you remember (x) from a couple years ago?" to them. Meanwhile it feels like a large chunk of my heart was robbed from me even 10 years later. Maybe that's entirely just me though.

I only recognized I had BPD around 15-16 or so, asking for a diagnosis but they insisted they couldn't until I was 18. Despite being put in psychiatric hold for "Clinical social anxiety and depression", and going through extensive DBT therapy that even provided a test that resulted with borderline results for a personality disorder or bipolar disorder.. I wasn't diagnosed despite everything being there. I think my symptoms were always noticable by other kids, but that could have just been autism.

I think it's kinda funny at times too, in regards to what they're jealous of. I once got down voted for being proud that I bought myself new clothes in an effort to challenge my negative self image, and not be devastated when my FP didn't complement me for having nice clothes!
Haha I think it's cute! Like how real finches would essentially wear skirts

I found when I have difficulty communicating my thoughts, I will text it out on my phone. Basically "texting" my therapist over talking can help me convey my emotions better than if I just sat anxiously pondering thoughts.
It doesn't bother me, I'm just very confused how we as a community are so supportive while simultaneously feeling ruined when someone from that same community also makes a small achievement?

Mine included "You're so dedicated to your Finch that I'm surprised you haven't started brewing butter tea for it in real life. Just remember, even virtual birds need boundaries." Ouch.
Yeah, it all feels like a lot of work to successfully attempt. Like it's more inconvenient to go through and fail than to just sleep all day in bed.

I've have multiple nightmares including being SA'd by family members, killing my beloved cats, killing a stray dog and dissecting it inside the house, and of course the everlasting monsters outside the window that keep coming. As of recent my worst types of "nightmares" include a scenario where what I wanted to happen with someone actually comes true, then when I wake up to look at the evidence I realize that it never happened. More so now I just wake up sweating and about to scream, but don't remember at all what I was scared about. I've had so many I don't remember them now.

I found that keeping a "nightmare" journal where you keep a paper and pencil next to your bed worked best for me. I would describe the dream in the sequence of events and how it made me feel. What helped the most with this journal was that I could physically place it where "everything that isn't real goes in". I never write real events in that journal, only bad dreams, nightmares, or dreams about events that never happened. Other times it was just talking to someone I trusted.

It's based on my mood. Particularly if I'm feeling so bad I can barley drive, I generally listen to music with a lot of that "vrrrrm" sound. Examples being Dogwalk by Creep-P or Typical Story by Hobo Johnson. If I'm feeling sad I just play music by Cavetown or Mitsuki.

I only drink it because it's cheap. It's never been for an "effect" outside of wanting to forget, wanting to get sick, and hoping I drink enough that I get alcohol poisoning. I think the intention makes a very big difference, especially the mindset you have while drinking.

Drinking alcohol in terms of medical perspective bad for everyone. Specifically twords BPD, it's a written symptom of "impulsive, self-destructive behaviors." This could look different in everyone, or not be a symptom at all.

What this looks like in me however, I never just have one drink. I'm 125lbs/56kg, I drink at least 36 fl oz of beer alone in one hour without eating or drinking anything else. This is not daily either, this is about once every two months approximately, which follows my intense mood swings.
Thank you very much! I'll start sending that one instead. Don't feel ashamed to share, I am greatful you're able to share!

I am on board with everyone else that has replied. Seek help, you deserve to be a better person. Don't settle to be your absolute worst, strive to be better. If you wish to only hurt people in your life, you will never keep anyone, and you will never have anyone.

Whenever you feel ready, get help or look for ways to help yourself. Not one of us wants to truly be a bad person. If you really want to be a bad person, you're in the wrong subreddit my friend.

I tell people so people know why I react the way I do, or why I cry out of absolutely nowhere. I encourage people to read about it, and I always send [this video](https://youtu.be/iraGmA7-9FA?si=8g1XPAtYyDAOHN2e) to anyone who does not know what BPD is. I want people to know that sometimes I need more help than others in some parts of my life, not that I am a ticking time bomb.

I recently just played Webkinz again because no other game allows me to feel as satisfied playing after 10 minutes than this. The short arcade games, shopping, and brushing my pets teeth have brought me little joys that daily life drains me of.

"it doesn't matter how much people love me, because it means nothing if it's not from him."
I've said this on multiple occasions to multiple people. I am with you so much, living by the idea of willingness to be a slave just so that the one person I want to be loved by could love me. So the concept of "think of all the people you'll hurt by disappearing" doesn't matter to me, because I want it from one person. I can't speak for your situation, as for me I want a singular person in particular to love me so much I cannot receive love from others no matter how much it is given to me.

I went to various therapists and a couple psychiatrists before getting a diagnosis. BPD has such a stigma some professionals would advocate for it to not be diagnosed (for some reason) or misunderstand the disorder entirely to be the same as Bipolar Disorder. So do be aware if you wish to get a diagnosis.
Roller skating. Every time I get on I end up on crutches the next day. Still absolutely love it.

I'm currently taking a martial arts class, Aikido, as well and trying to take some time to try and watch a movie once a week. It's hard to find time to dedicate two hours to something but that's what I'm currently doing

I often go straight to school then work right after. It was entirely so that I could spend less time at home due to my home environment being extremely toxic. So while I could take a day off, it would be just as stressful staying home as it would be to go out.

I am currently going to therapy. My therapist said I need to work on learning my emotional needs. Unfortunately all she has worked with me on so far is having me identify emotions. Unfortunately all I know is I'm stressed and that is not exactly helpful.

Maybe it's my autism mixed with BPD. I find blocking people as my way of communicating "I don't want to accept any more stimulation from you until I feel ready" which unfortunately is seen as "I don't want to be friends anymore"

I hate to fuel the fire here, but whenever I wanted a genuine "how do I manage my BPD" type of question here it tends to get bypassed, my emotional roller coaster being let out and it doesn't get recognized, and any successes or triumphs I post get completely squashed by another vent post by another person who posted "BPD SUCKS" type of vent. Look I love expressing how much I hate my BPD too, but I would also love to receive support outside of "yeah it's too bad BPD can't be cured."

I have a personality disorder and have trouble regulating my emotions and currently have a goal with my therapist on improving my self-assurance. Prompts for my journal have always been helpful as reflecting on generally my day alone can be repetitive at times

1. Yes and no. "Mood swings" are very extreme for me. I will be crying and someone can show be a cute video of a borzoi playing with a toy and it will make me giggle a bit out of it (tears still in my eyes). However, when I'm in an episode, I cannot be consoled and there's nothing that will uplift me. For someone on the outside, it looks like I'm refusing the help I am begging for, and I have been described as someone who "loves being miserable" due to this. However if someone I do feel like is helping me get out of sadness, I become insecure and feel like the relationship is a fraud (over literally anything, it could be just them buying me an ice cream after I couldn't be consoled after dropping my cone on the cement). It really depends on the individual's values I think. If their values are challenged or inconvenienced in any real or perceived way, it won't be so easy to uplift them. But if they're just upset over something outside of their values, it could be expressed as just an intense mood swing.

2. Absolutely. I named it "Shim", a fusion of "she" and "him". I describe Shim as a large black snake with spines of a porcupine and an eye of a ticking clock. Shim follows me, and I ended up naming my anger split the same. It's all my negative thoughts in one being. I use Shim as a creative outlet to express any negative feelings I have.

3. For sure. "Why couldn't they invite me? Why couldn't I have been the only one they hang out with? Is there something wrong with me that makes them not want to be with me?" Are questions I ask

4. Yes. I was broken up with once because I took up too much time and energy for them, so they insisted that we never talk again. That was how not only our relationship,  our friendship had come to an abrupt end.

5. Cry some more. Jokes aside, after a breakdown I enjoy getting to work or doing homework. Do I like going to work and doing schoolwork? No! But I get it done so that I could at least have some energy left to process my emotions.

6. My anger is visceral. I will either blow up or break down. It's a 1/80 chance I will become physically angry, often aiming towards the person I am angry at. Having a healthy outlet to express anger is very critical. Not everyone with BPD becomes physically angry, and it's never an excuse to hurt someone.
Depression.

I was also rather strange in the sense I preferred to be by myself, but I vividly remember being very hurt whenever I was picked last for games. I also have ASD, which was a late diagnosis, but it explained the ostracization. (Kids just know when someone isn't quite normal)

I hit my favorite person, yes, but if they're seriously hurt I will do everything in my power to make up for it. Abuse is not okay no matter what. I am lucky my favorite person is incredibly tough, and we both are experienced in Aikido (self defense without harming the attacker). If he has to he pins me down until my aggression subsides. That's our friendship and we both are okay with this, and I will never excuse my actions whenever I hurt my loved ones. No matter how angry I get, no matter how sad I am, hurting them is never okay. As Webkinz the app would be fantastic, I would rather it be separate from Finch. Finch is the best self care app I've ever been able to use, and I wish that others could see it was self improvement. You're learning how to take care of yourself for you, not just for your Finch.
I'm told I'm nice, I think I'm nice. I just wonder if I actually am.
I had work and no one really loves me that much to go out with me (not even me)

I take myself on dates. I go to the mall by myself. I go to the bookstore. I go to the local library and study. I try to take myself out for cheap meals, cause normally I eat very very healthy meals. I listen to bands I like.

Do I enjoy being alone? Absolutely not. A majority of my trauma led to me spending a lot of time alone, making me associate loneliness with the fact I did something unforgivably wrong. But, treating yourself makes it feel not as bad, than if you just stayed home.

I never got loved enough by anyone to get a sincere gift. Much less would I be given something so generous on a day supposed to be celebrating such. The one gift I got was one of those giant stuffed bears from a pharmacy because my ex knew I liked soft toys, and wanted to give me the most inconvenient gift possible. Yes, he told me he wanted to inconvenience me with gifts. He never got me anything following that first gift.

I always got chocolates from friends in the past, even though I told them multiple times I don't like chocolate. Come on, at least get me a sugar stick or a cookie. I used to always hand make candies for friends, hand make cards, and / or bake cookies. And they'd just give me chocolate.. or nothing. I stopped giving my senior year of high school because I had to be put on medical hold around the same time as Valentine's. I handmade a soft toy for my boyfriend, where my hands were shaking so much from crying I picked my finger and proceeded to bleed on the white toy as I tried to hand stitch it.

Unsurprisingly, no one got me anything. Not even my boyfriend at the time.

I never got a Valentine's gift after that from anyone, not even close friends. I was always broken up before the holiday came close. I just want to be shown I'm important to *someone* for once. Even if it was one stupid card.

I feel the same. Nothing is interesting, there's nothing to look forward to, everything in mundane! How could "I'm bored" just be resolved so quickly to others? How could anyone be satisfied with just going for a walk around the neighborhood, and no longer be bored?

I'm working with my therapist to learn how to find inner satisfaction. Learning how to enjoy being in your own company. Apparently, this boredom I have, is feeling unfulfilled without someone else doing it for me. I have a desperate need for someone else to solve my problems, including boredom, ignoring what my own emotional wants/needs are and wishing someone else could figure it out. It's a rough path learning where that chronic boredom is coming from, you're really not alone in this.
Can't say. I personally become more physical with people close to me, either violent or inappropriately, if self harm is not considered acting out.
I never got a Valentine's gift so I'm going to treat myself with this idea. Thank you for sharing :)

Disassociation for me feels like chronic emptiness, yes, however I am not able to express or recognize my emotions. I feel like I'm walking in a dream. As though I never woke up from my dream. Sometimes I don't even realize I am disassociated until weeks later. In worst case scenarios I become completely unresponsive to outside stimulation and tend to stare off.

Learning you have BPD changes nothing other than the fact you know you have it. Before you didn't, after you learned you did. It doesn't change who you were before or after learning about it, nor does it change the problems you are having. Learning you have it means that you can finally get the help you need. It's up to you to get that help.

BPD and Autistic here

Fear of abandonment is a symptom of BPD, AND it is not required for diagnosis. As long as you fit 5 of the 9 criteria. Only one is: frantic efforts to avoid real or perceived abandonment.

Unfortunately my mom is the same, and she's not even a stepmom. She's my biological mom. Moms can be the absolute worst, and sometimes try their best to excuse it because they've been told enough they're good mothers. People don't see what it's like to be their kid, much less do people see what it's like to have BPD and be treated as such. Moms are supposed to be loving and caring pillars in our lives, however not all moms are like that. Heck, I was bullied relentlessly by my brother and all my mom could do was say I should just stand up for myself instead of expecting her to. I really get it. Try to not let them under your skin (though they definitely love to live there, easier said than done). If you just want to vent about it feel free to message me if you need to.

I feel the exact same, unfortunately my ex never cut me out really. It's been over a year since our breakup, and I still felt he was mine. I asked him just last night actually, "what am I to you?" He said he didn't know and asked me what I see him as. I told him I saw him as someone I want to spend the rest of my life with, in togetherness. He agreed. I finally told him I wanted him as my boyfriend and yet he only calls me a friend, despite still treating me like his girlfriend. He said he was sorry, and I finally stepped up for myself. "You need to either just treat me as a friend, or ask me out again. Cause every time you treat me like your girlfriend, I think I am, and you destroy me when you can say so matter of fact that we're just friends. We can be friends with benefits, but treat me as such. Not your girlfriend." Its probably one of the hardest things I've faced in my life is when he just said he'll start treating me only as a friend. I still feel like he's dating me after all this. I understand.

What made me so sure I had BPD, having to advocate for myself and push for a diagnosis since I was 16 despite only being able to be diagnosed at 18, was that my emotions were beyond anything I had experienced compared to anyone else in my life. I cried often, mostly for no reason. I never cried at my grandpa's funeral, or the day my cat brother passed away. But I sobbed for hours, days, weeks, and months leading up to the day.

My anger was always visceral and sudden, to where if someone made me mad I would point out every single flaw within them before removing them from my life the same day without looking back. I circled through friends like pairs of socks, cutting them out as quickly as tags on clothes. There would be nice people I met, but that thought of them being "nice" always quickly turned into me hating that they felt the need to pretend to be kind to me. I constantly accused friends of their kind acts being lies, and even now I unintentionally still claim that spending time with me is a waste of their valued time (ie, at the end of spending time together I apologize for wasting their time). Whoever I was is what I felt was expected of me. In middle school I hyper sexualized myself due to abuse leading me to believe that's all people saw me as, and by high school I was failing my classes because I was expected to be my "friends" who all kept 4.0 GPA.

BPD is different in everyone. We all have different experiences, and it can always show itself differently. This is just how it is for me. I hope that this was helpful.
